newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA TAKES BLAME, SAYS WINDIES WILL BE BACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA TAKES BLAME, SAYS WINDIES WILL BE BACK.

text.p: Star batsman Brian Lara blames his own poor form for the West Indies' recent seven-match losing streak but says his team can still salvage their disastrous tour of Australia.

The West Indies were soundly beaten in the first two tests against Australia and lost two of their first three matches in the World Series limited overs tournament. Lara, who holds the world record for the highest test and first-class scores, turned in a string of disappointing performances.
But Lara was quoted in Australian newspapers on Thursday as saying that the West Indies could still win the five-test series against Australia.
He said the seven-wicket defeat of Pakistan in a World Series match on Tuesday had boosted the team ahead of the third test starting in Melbourne on December 26.
"We needed a result like that, an emphatic win," Lara said.
"The guys bowled well, batted well and fielded well. Hopefully, this will give the guys the lift we need for the third test match.
"We are 2-0 down but there are three to go and we can still win the series. I think we can take it from here.
"We are going to pick this up and be successful before the end of the tour," he said.
Lara, who had been silent for most of the tour to date, said his own form had contributed to the side's slump.
"I've been worried knowing the team hasn't been doing very well," Lara told Sydney's The Daily Telegraph.

"They needed me and I'm not scoring runs. I'm not overly worried if I'm not scoring runs and the team is doing well, but I think my failures have been part of the problems the team has been having," he said.
West Indies' team morale had been "very low" and they were "really down in the dumps", Lara said on the eve of a four-day match against state side Victoria which started on Thursday.
Lara was disciplined by West Indies' team management after storming into the Australian dressing room and confronting team officials after he was dismissed during the second test.
The 27-year-old left-hander said the incident displayed his own competitive character.
"The West Indies know they're not going to get a person who's quiet and laid-back," he said.
